findings.title: Clear pending windows when flushing a batch
findings.comment: In /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/aggregate.py, adding one row and calling flush() leaves open_window_count() at 1, and a second flush() emits the identical row again. Thus summarize_files([a, b]) re-emits a's windows in b, merges same-key statistics across batches, and retains all prior aggregate state despite the documented emit-and-retire and bounded-backfill contracts.

findings.title: Subtract allowed lateness from the tenant watermark
findings.comment: In /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/windows.py:70, cutoff is watermark + allowed_lateness. With watermark 100 and allowance 30, timestamp 110 is incorrectly dropped as 110 < 130, as is timestamp 90 even though it is only 10 seconds behind. The documented semantics require dropping only timestamps below watermark - allowance (below 70 here), with timestamp 70 accepted.

findings.title: Load tenant configuration outside the per-reading loop
findings.comment: The loop at /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/pipeline.py:39-40 invokes load_tenant_limits for every reading, and that function opens and parses tenants.json each time. A five-reading reproduction made five loads, so a 100,000-reading single-tenant batch makes 100,000 unchanged configuration reads rather than in-memory lookups.

findings.title: Validate max_value before converting it
findings.comment: In /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/tenants.py:55, configs with acme.max_value equal to "bad", [], or {} raise ValueError/TypeError and abort ingest, despite the surrounding normalization policy that malformed tenant entries should degrade to no limit. A value of "NaN" instead returns max_value=nan, for which every reading.value > max_value comparison is false, leaving a non-finite and ineffective configured limit.

findings.title: Distinguish an absent tenant from an explicit null entry
findings.comment: With config {"default":{"max_value":10},"acme":null}, /tmp/native-review-smoke/case1/tenants.py returns TenantLimits("acme", 10.0), so an acme reading above 10 is clipped. The documented rule only makes an absent tenant inherit default, while the subsequent non-mapping normalization says malformed explicit entries become no-limit; config.get conflates the present null entry with absence.

coverage.lens: Inspect per-tenant watermark arithmetic and state carryover across batches, especially the allowed-lateness boundary.
Check that batch flushing actually retires aggregate state and that each emitted batch contains only its own windows.
Examine tenant-limit configuration loading for fallback and malformed-value behavior, and for per-reading file-I/O costs.
